message.content: The lion (Panthera leo) and the zebra (Equus quagga) belong to very different mammalian orders—Carnivora and Perissodactyla, respectively. Their most recent common ancestor is therefore a very early placental mammal that lived roughly 70–80 million years ago, long before the diversification of the modern orders. This ancestor would have been a small, insectivorous mammal that lived in the Paleocene–Eocene epochs, and it is the last common ancestor of all placental mammals (excluding marsupials and monotremes).
